title: Dhurandhar's marketing head Varun Gupta reveals why Ranveer Singh didn't promote film, recalls Aditya Dhar's calm reaction to criticism before release
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Aditya Dhar and Ranveer Singh 's Dhurandhar became a major box-office success, breaking several records and establishing itself as one of the highest-grossing Indian movie franchises. However, before its rollout, the movie faced criticism over its marketing strategy, with some followers expressing disappointment over the lack of buzz. In a conversation with the Everyday Empires podcast, Varun Gupta, founder of Max Marketing, the agency behind the promotional campaigns for Dhurandhar and Dhurandhar: The Revenge, revealed why Ranveer did not promote the movie and recalled Aditya's reaction to the criticism before its rollout.

Adding to this, Dhurandhar's marketing agency founder reveals why Ranveer Singh didn't promote the movie. Varun Gupta on Dhurandhar's marketing strategy Varun shared he could not recall any Hindi movie releasing a 3.5-minute-long promotional asset six months before its rollout prior to Dhurandhar. He added that while such a practice was common in Hollywood, it had not been seen in Hindi cinema. He also opened up that his team came on board for Dhurandhar even before the star cast was finalised and heard the script at that stage.
Meanwhile, He shared that while the movie is now being hailed as a major success, the team faced criticism before its rollout, with people questioning its marketing, promotions and lack of buzz.

Notably, He shared, "There were times when articles would come out saying the promotions were bad and there was no buzz. Aditya would just send them to me and say, ‘It’s all okay.’ There were no questions asked. That kind of trust makes you want to do anything for them. You become their warriors. I’m happy the movie worked because everyone put a lot into it. But Aditya and Ranveer Singh, specifically, put in a lot beyond what they should have as a director and an star. I’m happy for everyone associated with it."

As per the latest buzz, Varun also spoke about the alleged paid smear campaigns targeting films ahead of their rollout. He shared that when a movie starring a particular star is about to rollout, certain sections unnecessarily criticise it. He pointed out that filmmakers face criticism regardless of whether they take the lead star out for promotions. If the star participates in promotional activities, people question why such a big star needs to promote the movie and argue that newer actors would attract more attention. However, if the star does not participate, people claim that the makers are promoting the movie without generating enough buzz.
In further updates, Varun also explained why Ranveer did not promote Dhurandhar, contrasting the decision with Ranbir Kapoor's promotional activities for Animal.

On top of that, He shared, "Ranbir had Tu Jhoothi Main Makkaar before Animal rolled out, Ranveer Singh had not had a great run before Dhurandhar. There was a very conscious decision between us, the director, the producer and the star. We were like, ‘Okay, let the movie and its assets talk. Let the actors not talk.'"

Varun's company has previously worked on promotional campaigns for films such as RRR, Animal, Kalki 2898 AD and Chandu Champion. It is also associated with SS Rajamouli's soon-to-release movie Varanasi, starring Mahesh Babu, Priyanka Chopra and Prithviraj Sukumaran in lead roles.

title: Marco Rubio dismisses question on India protests as domestic matter, calls ‘UN experts’ an oxymoron
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

US secretary of state Marco Rubio described the Cockroach Janta Party-led protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as India's "domestic matter", while calling UN experts an "oxymoron" over their criticism of the police response to the demonstrations.

Adding to this, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will be visiting Gujarat's Jamnagar on Wednesday to complete his second trip to India in four months (REUTERS) Reacting to the remarks made by UN experts on the CJP protests and the police response, Rubio shared, “Oh, UN experts, my favourite. The UN experts are the oxymoron.”

Meanwhile, “It is a domestic political matter. I am not going to comment on it. This is a democracy, they have elections here. I am not going to opine on their domestic, political matters. We have protests every day in US,” shared Rubio while talking to reporters.

Notably, UN experts had criticised the Indian police's “heavy-handed” response to youth-led demonstrations in Delhi. They urged the authorities to protect peaceful protests and ensure justice for alleged human rights violations during these and earlier demonstrations.

In further updates, More than 20 UN human rights experts in Geneva had expressed alarm over what they called a "repeatedly heavy-handed police response" to youth-led protests in the national capital.

On top of that, She shared, “Human rights should not be used as an instrument of political pressure or selective country targeting. India engages with international human rights mechanisms, but such engagement must be based on dialogue, consultation and cooperation, with non-selectivity and transparency as guiding principles.”

Tamrakar shared India was willing to address specific cases supported by proper documentation through established channels. However, she opposed any “attempt to convert unverified allegations, incomplete statistics or a report that contains no India country observation into a negative characterisation of the world's largest democracy”.

title: Police Company release date: Ram Gopal Varma’s crime saga starring Harshvardhan Rane to hit theatres on June 4, 2027
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Harshvardhan Rane will portray Mumbai encounter specialist Daya Nayak in the action thriller, which also features Fardeen Khan, Fatima Sana Shaikh and others.

Adding to this, Known for exploring the underbelly of Mumbai through films like Satya and Company , Ram Gopal Varma is revisiting familiar territory with a narrative that shifts the focus from gangsters to the police officers who confronted them. In Police Company , Harshvardhan Rane will portray Daya Nayak, the Mumbai police encounter specialist whose operations became a significant part of the city’s underworld history.

Meanwhile, Inspired by true events and real-life police officers who operated during the late 1990s and early 2000s, the movie will delve into the functioning of Mumbai’s encounter squad during a particularly volatile period. The narrative is expected to explore the circumstances, aggressive policing tactics and high-stakes operations that shaped the battle against organised crime in the financial capital.

Notably, The movie will revisit an era when gang-related violence and the underworld’s influence formed a significant part of Mumbai’s crime landscape. According to the movie’s announcement, the story will trace the operations through which the encounter squad neutralised around 300 gangsters, eventually dismantling the underworld’s terror network in the city. By placing law enforcement at the centre of the narrative, Police Company aims to offer a different perspective on a chapter that has frequently inspired crime dramas in Hindi cinema.

As per the latest buzz, Alongside Harshvardhan Rane, Police Company features Fardeen Khan, Fatima Sana Shaikh, Paresh Rawal, Saurabh Shukla, Makarand Deshpande and Ashwini Kalsekar in pivotal roles. The ensemble brings together several established performers, including actors who have previously been associated with Ram Gopal Varma’s distinctive brand of crime cinema.

In further updates, The casting also marks a creative reunion for several veteran actors whose work has contributed to Varma’s crime-movie legacy over the decades. Their presence adds to the movie’s focus on an intense, character-driven narrative set against the backdrop of Mumbai’s underworld and the police operations mounted against it.

On top of that, Presented by Gulshan Kumar and T-Series, Police Company is directed by Ram Gopal Varma and produced by Bhushan Kumar, Krishan Kumar and Ram Gopal Varma. The movie is being made under the banners of T-Series Films and RGV Company Production.

With its real-life inspiration, portrayal of a defining period in Mumbai’s underworld history and Harshvardhan Rane stepping into the role of Daya Nayak, Police Company marks Varma’s return to a genre closely associated with his filmography. The crime drama is slated for a nationwide theatrical rollout on June 4, 2027.

body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

The advance booking for Ramayana , starring Ranbir Kapoor and Yash , opened on October 20, coinciding with Dussehra. Within 24 hours, the highly anticipated movie has recorded an encouraging start, with advance bookings worth over ₹ 3 crore rupees across India, 15 days before its theatrical rollout. Here's a look at the movie's day 1 advance booking figures ahead of its November 5 rollout.

Adding to this, Ramayana's Hindi screenings account for about 95% of the gross, while bookings for Tamil and Telugu shows have yet to open. Ramayana advance booking day 1 According to Sacnilk, Ramayana has collected ₹ 3.13 crore rupees in advance bookings, excluding blocked seats. The movie has sold 86,187 tickets across 3,537 shows in 104 cities. Its current occupancy stands at 11%.

Meanwhile, On BookMyShow, advance bookings for the November 5 rollout are filling up quickly in the limited shows that have opened across cities. In New Delhi, some morning shows, including the 7:10 am screenings, have only a few seats left. In Mumbai, the PVR Phoenix Palladium IMAX screening, with tickets priced at ₹ 2,770, is sold out, while another tickets, priced at ₹ 1,550, is almost full.

Notably, The Hindi version is driving the movie's advance booking, accounting for around 95% of its gross collection through 3,474 shows. The Kannada market has also shown early interest, contributing around ₹ 25 lakh through 61 shows. The makers appear to be tapping into Yash's popularity in Karnataka, although only a limited number of Kannada shows have opened for advance booking so far. Bookings for Tamil and Telugu shows have yet to open.

In the first 24 hours of advance booking, Dhurandhar: The Revenge collected ₹ 7.80 crore rupees for its opening day, excluding blocked seats.

In further updates, In comparison, Ramayana has collected ₹ 3.13 crore rupees without blocked seats in the first 24 hours of advance booking. However, with more shows expected to open, the movie's advance booking figures could change as its rollout date approaches.

On top of that, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana is an adaptation of the Hindu epic of the same name. title: Anupam Kher backs Daler Mehndi, says minister publicly ‘insulting’ singer was unfair
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Punjabi singer Daler Mehndi has received support from star Anupam Kher amid the row surrounding his performance at a cultural event in Uttarakhand. The row erupted after state Cabinet minister Subodh Uniyal publicly reprimanded the singer during the Maa Kunjapuri Mela in Tehri Garhwal, accusing him of performing after consuming alcohol. After the video went widely shared, Daler's brother Mika Singh, comedian Kapil Sharma and singer Badshah came out in his support. Anupam has now defended the singer and urged members of the movie industry to speak up for him.

Adding to this, Anupam Kher defends Daler Mehndi, says singer has been unwell for 2-3 years. Anupam Kher backs Daler Mehndi On Wednesday, Anupam posted on Instagram to share a video in support of Daler. Revealing that he was currently abroad, the star shared he had watched the video of the singer's performance. He shared he had known Daler for 25-30 years and vouched for his character, adding that the singer did not drink and was one of the finest human beings he knew.

Meanwhile, Anupam also shared that Daler had been unwell for the past two to three years and shared he knew this through a doctor they both knew. He suggested that the singer might have had prior commitments to the event organisers and had chosen to honour them despite his health concerns.

Notably, "I can say he doesn't drink and he's one of the finest human beings. He is not well, and I personally know this because we have a common friend, a doctor, and I have met him there several times. He has been ill for 2-3 years. Maybe he had earlier commitments with the organisation and he couldn't say no to them; that's his professionalism, that he stuck with his commitment," Anupam shared.
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Anupam Kher (@anupampkher)
In further updates, He further urged members of the movie industry to stand up for Daler, arguing that even if the singer had lip-synced, he did not deserve to be reprimanded publicly.

On top of that, "Maybe he did lip-sync, but nobody should speak to anyone like that. That too on a public forum, it's not fair. To put allegations on someone like this is wrong. I think our industry should talk about this; it's not only Mika Singh's responsibility to defend his brother. We should all take a stand for the people that we know. I felt bad, and I want to tell you, Daler ji, that I trust your judgement, professionalism and your greatness and may God bless you and you get well soon. I am sorry you had to go through this," he added.

Alongside the video, Anupam also shared a caption in which he questioned the minister's decision to reprimand Daler publicly. He acknowledged that the minister may have had concerns about the performance but argued that the issue could have been addressed privately and respectfully.

title: As actors get more physical, Bollywood embraces intimacy coordinators
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

India's movie industry, where scenes featuring nudity or sex often rely on improvisation and mutual trust, is gradually welcoming professionals tasked with choreographing intimacy to protect actors and ensure consent.

Adding to this, As actors get more physical, Bollywood embraces intimacy coordinators Once unheard-of in Bollywood, intimacy coordinators are becoming an increasingly familiar presence on sets as filmmakers embrace stricter standards after the #MeToo movement put a spotlight on sexual exploitation in entertainment industries around the world.
Meanwhile, The shift comes as streaming platforms have pushed storytelling into a more nuanced territory, creating greater demand for realistic portrayals of sexuality.

Notably, "Just like a stunt director handles a fight scene... for scenes of intimacy, we map out exactly where the hand goes and where the hair goes so nothing is left to awkward improvisation," shared Aastha Khanna, one of a small but growing group of intimacy coordinators in Bollywood.
As per the latest buzz, Most arrive on set armed with "modesty tools" that allow performers to simulate intimacy while minimising unnecessary physical contact.

In further updates, The emergence of such coordinators reflects a broader transformation in an industry where intimate scenes traditionally relied on trust between actors and directors, often with few formal safeguards.
On top of that, Khanna shared coordinators are usually hired before casting begins.
"The idea is that actors know there are intimate scenes in the script and can decide whether they are comfortable with them before signing on," she told AFP.

title: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi's Ramayana made tax-free in West Bengal ahead of release, CM Suvendu Adhikari announces on Dussehra
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Nitesh Tiwari 's ambitious adaptation of the Hindu epic Ramayana, starring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama and Yash as Ravana, has been made tax-free in West Bengal. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari made the announcement on Dussehra, ahead of the movie's theatrical rollout on November 5, 2026.

Adding to this, Ramayana will rollout worldwide on November 5. Ramayana revealed tax-free in West Bengal In conversation with ANI on Tuesday, Adhikari shared, "The Ramayana movie has been made tax-free. The Kerala Story, The Kashmir Files, and The Bengal Files—all of these will be (or have been) made tax-free, and the same will apply to Ramayana. In the days to come, we will see films on Shri Krishna and Arjuna, as well as the Mahabharata..."

Meanwhile, The Chief Minister also expressed grief over the stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata's Chorbagan area. He shared, "We also carry a deep pain in our hearts regarding the incident at the Durga Puja pandal in Chorbagan area. From this very stage, we offered prayers for those affected as well. We observed a moment of silence. Everyone stands with the grieving family."

Notably, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and backed by Namit Malhotra, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Yash as Ravana, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Ravi Dubey as Lakshman and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The movie also features Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Arun Govil, Lara Dutta, Sheeba Chaddha, Shobana and Faisal Malik, among others, in key roles.
As per the latest buzz, Mounted on a reported budget of ₹ 4,000 crore rupees for its two parts, the movie is being planned as an ambitious cinematic adaptation of the Indian epic.

In further updates, When the makers unveiled the movie's first look, featuring Ranbir as Lord Rama, it received mixed reactions online. While some viewers questioned the star's casting, others criticised the visual effects. However, the movie's subsequent trailer received a more positive response from many viewers, with some noting the improvements made by the makers following audience feedback.

On top of that, The movie's distribution plans include Dil Raju in the Telugu-speaking states, Karan Johar in the Hindi-speaking market and Sony Pictures for its international rollout, according to the information provided.

Backed by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios, Yash's Monster Mind Creations and DNEG, the movie is planned as a two-part rollout. The first part is scheduled to arrive in theatres on November 5, 2026, coinciding with Diwali.

title: UN experts slam India’s ‘heavy-handed’ crackdown on youth-led protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

United Nations’ experts have criticised the Indian police’s “heavy-handed” response to youth-led protests in Delhi and elsewhere over the past three months, urging authorities to protect peaceful agitations and ensure justice for alleged rights violations during these and earlier demonstrations.

Adding to this, Security personnel detain a National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) worker during their protest against the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, demanding his resignation near the NSUI headquarters, in New Delhi. (ANI) “This crackdown reflects a broader, troubling pattern,” the experts shared in a note issued in Geneva on Tuesday. “We have repeatedly alerted the Indian authorities to undue restrictions on peaceful assembly, excessive use of force, arbitrary detentions, enforced disappearances, and the targeting of student activists, amongst others.”
Meanwhile, There was no immediate reaction from the Indian government or authorities at the time of filing this report.

Notably, The statement comes as the protests, which began over government decisions on the education system, have widened into a sustained challenge to the Union government. The latest trigger is the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

As per the latest buzz, The experts shared the SIR process affects 130 million people, or 13 crore rupees, a number roughly equal to the population of Mexico. They shared those affected as per reports belong to the Muslim minority, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

In further updates, The unrest over the SIR has gathered pace since late September, after reports that two deputies of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar raised internal concerns about the exercise. The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party and student groups have sought Kumar’s resignation and a halt to the SIR exercise. They have described their latest phase of protests as “Season 2”.

On top of that, However, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) at the Centre and the Election Commission have denied any manipulation of the rolls, and the BJP has defended the revision as a clean-up of voter lists. Opposition parties and several independent analysts have also alleged the Muslims have been disproportionately affected, though researchers note that religion-wise data has not been published, so such estimates rest on name analysis.

India has also pushed back against international criticism. Earlier this month, the Ministry of External Affairs called a UN statement on the protests selective and an “unwarranted interference in the internal affairs of India”.

title: Society, not protests, can trigger change: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat on Tuesday shared that andolan, or agitation, does not bring about change; and solutions to problems often come from within society, adding that when protests are political or instigated, they can create tension and anarchy, and disrupt public order.

Adding to this, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat in Nagpur on Tuesday. (HT Photo) “Experience shows that it is neither the government alone that can resolve all the problems of society, nor is it true that problems can be resolved only through agitations. Solutions can also emerge through the active participation of the society and dialogue among its members,” Bhagwat shared, delivering the annual Vijaydashami lecture in Nagpur .

Meanwhile, The RSS chief’s comments come against the backdrop of ongoing street protests by the Opposition and the Cockroach Janta Party demanding electoral reforms and the removal of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the conduct of the special intensive revision (SIR) .
Notably, The Opposition, particularly the Congress, has accused the poll panel of working at the behest of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party , the political arm of the Sangh.
As per the latest buzz, The RSS chief shared that the people of India needed to be cautious that there were forces in the West that wanted India derailed from its path of becoming a developed nation.

In further updates, “ A storm has swept in from the West, driven by a demonic resolve to destroy and devastate all that is decent, auspicious, and rooted in cultural and human values, both in Bharat and across the world. Even the so-called developed nations across the world are afflicted by this storm and find themselves helpless before it. However, over the past decades, Bharat has gradually carved out a place for itself in the world through its own strength and sound policies,” he shared.
On top of that, He cited France , Albania, Nepaland Bangladesh as examples of foreign interference that tried to push regime change as a means of finding solutions.

“Look at what has been happening in France, Albania, Nepal and Bangladesh in recent days. They want to make similar attempts in Bharat as well. But a change of regime does not change anything. Look at the situation there,” he shared.

title: ‘Doosra, Delhi Belly both got A certificates’: Filmmaker Abhinay Deo says he has never fought with CBFC, reveals his experience with the board | Excl
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

When Sourav Ganguly took off his shirt and waved it from the Lord’s balcony after India’s memorable NatWest Series victory in 2002, it became one of the defining moments in Indian cricket. While the celebration is remembered for its sheer audacity, filmmaker Abhinay Deo sees it as a statement of confidence from a team that was no longer willing to play second fiddle. That spirit of defiance forms the heart of his soon-to-release movie Doosra, which connects the Indian cricketer’s rebellious streak with the story of Tara, a young woman growing up in a conservative household in Rajasthan who begins questioning the restrictions imposed on her.

Adding to this, Filmmaker Abhinay Deo says he has never fought with the CBFC, recalls getting A certificates for Doosra and Delhi Belly. Starring Plabita Borthakur as Tara, the movie uses a landmark moment in cricket to explore a much more personal struggle for freedom. Beyond its central theme, the movie has also received an A certificate from the Central Board of Movie Certification (CBFC), raising questions about how filmmakers navigate the certification process while trying to preserve their stories. Abhinay, however, says his experience with the board has been largely hassle-free, unlike the challenges other filmmakers have spoken about.

Meanwhile, According to several reports, CBFC flagged a few scenes in Doosra, including a brief shot of a nude photograph in an adult magazine that Tara's father catches her looking at as a child. The board also raised concerns about a reference to the Babri Masjid episode and sought changes to the scene. However, director Abhinay Deo was reluctant to alter footage he considered important to the story and chose to accept an A certificate instead of making the requested cuts.

Notably, Abhinay points to his 2011 dark comedy Delhi Belly as an example of how smoothly the certification process has worked for him. In conversation with Hindustan Times, he says, “My experience with anything that could be considered objectionable goes back to Delhi Belly, my first movie, and now Doosra, my latest movie. Interestingly, both films were adult-rated, and both were passed without cuts. My meeting with the board lasted seven or eight minutes, maybe ten. They asked what rating I was expecting, and I shared a U/A rating would be great, but if that meant cuts, I would rather go without them.”

As per the latest buzz, He explains that the board asked him to change just one word in Doosra, much as it had done with Delhi Belly. “It’s a very interesting story because both my films were adult-rated with just one word changed. I have never had a fight with them,” he adds.

In further updates, Abhinay is quick to clarify that his experience may not reflect what other filmmakers have gone through. For Doosra, he says, the team was comfortable with an A certificate because it felt the movie was not necessarily meant for younger viewers to watch on their own. However, he believes its themes could still resonate with them. “We were very clear that we were fine with an adult certification. This is not a movie for a 13-year-old to come and watch on their own, though it is a very important movie for a 13-year-old to see as well,” he explains. He adds that he has no issue with the movie eventually reaching audiences on a streaming platform.

On top of that, At around 78 minutes, Doosra is considerably shorter than most mainstream theatrical releases. Abhinay believes the movie's length and intense storytelling make it well suited to a continuous screening without an interval. While the team had hoped to avoid a break, the director admits that the final decision is not entirely in their hands.

“In a 78-minute movie that is an intense drama, I think it can very easily go without a break. There are some films where the first half itself is longer than 78 minutes these days,” he says. While he understands that exhibitors have commercial considerations, including selling refreshments during intervals, he believes the movie's viewing experience deserves equal consideration. “I understand that they need to sell popcorn, but at the end of the day, they exist because of films. They need to be a little more sensitive towards the films as well,” he explains.

title: ‘So much blood and mayhem’: Shashi Tharoor reviews Ranveer Singh's Dhurandhar, questions propaganda, gruesome violence and portrayal of India-Pakistan
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Congress Member of Parliament Shashi Tharoor has lauded Ranveer Singh ’s Dhurandhar films for their filmmaking and performances, but he has reservations about the violence and political messaging in the franchise. After watching both parts of Aditya Dhar ’s spy thriller, the politician shared he enjoyed the sequel Dhurandhar: The Revenge more than the first movie. However, he felt several violent scenes were unnecessarily graphic and questioned how the films portray India-Pakistan relations. The two installments, rolled out in December 2025 and March 2026, have as per reports collected more than ₹ 3,100 crore rupees worldwide.

Adding to this, Congress Member of Parliament Shashi Tharoor has lauded Ranveer Singh’s Dhurandhar films for their filmmaking and performances, but he has reservations about the violence and political messaging in the franchise. Shashi Tharoor says Dhurandhar 2 is better than the first movie In an almost seven minute video posted on his official YouTube channel, Shashi shared his thoughts on both films and made it clear that the second instalment stood out for him. “As a work of fiction, as a work of entertainment, there is no doubt that the second part is superb,” he shared.

Meanwhile, While he appreciated the sequel as a work of entertainment, he was critical of the violence shown in the franchise. He felt the filmmakers could have told the story without relying on so many disturbing scenes. “There was no need to show so much violence, blood, mayhem, cruelty and some of the most disgusting scenes ever seen in Indian cinema,” he added, describing the graphic content as “totally excessive and over the top.”

Notably, The Congress MP also spoke about the political messaging in Dhurandhar. The films have faced criticism over their portrayal of Pakistan, and Shashi acknowledged that such themes could influence how audiences view the relationship between the two countries. He referred to reports of bans in Pakistan and several Gulf nations, where concerns were as per reports raised about the films potentially worsening tensions between Indians and Pakistanis.

As per the latest buzz, “Things that I don't like; there is far too much gruesome violence. It was totally excessive and over the top. There was no need to show so much of violence, blood and mayhem, cruelty and some of the most disgusting scenes ever seen in Indian cinema,” he shared. “There is a lot of propaganda stuff built into it obviously and I gather the movie has been banned in many countries, not just in Pakistan, but many of the Gulf countries have banned it, saying it would needlessly create bad blood between Indians and Pakistanis, so I can understand those feelings,” the politician added.

In further updates, He also wondered how Pakistani viewers might react if they watched the films. He suggested that some dialogues might be received with humour, while other parts could lead audiences to reflect on actions carried out in their country's name. “I don’t know how Pakistanis will react if they see this. Some of the lines, I think Pakistanis will laugh. Some of the other things, I think Pakistanis will realise how much wrong has been done in their name,” he went onto say.

On top of that, Dhurandhar follows an undercover intelligence operative Jaskirat Singh Rangi alias Hamza Ali Mazari, with the story featuring secret missions and high-stakes operations. Shashi shared his own interactions with intelligence officials had been very different from what the films show. He explained that his experience involved discussions, analysis and sharing information, rather than the dramatic, covert operations depicted on screen.

“I have dealt with a lot of our intelligence people but in a very civilised way, having analysis, conversations, information exchanges but not really getting into any cloak and dagger stuff. I am certainly not aware of commands being given that lead to explosions in faraway capitals. That’s not the world I have ever lived in,” he explained.

Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram While the photographs captured a peaceful moment, a video from their visit has since gone widely shared on the internet. The clip shows Sara appearing visibly overwhelmed with emotion, moved to tears as she stood in prayer at the Darbar Sahib.

Notably, View this post on Instagram All about Udta Teer The Golden Temple visit comes ahead of the rollout of Udta Teer, which is scheduled to arrive in theatres on October 23. The movie was initially set to rollout on October 9 before its date was pushed back.

As per the latest buzz, The movie marks the directorial debut of Akash A Kaushik and brings together a sizeable ensemble cast. Along with Sara and Ayushmann in the lead roles, it features Rahul Bose, Ram Kapoor, Suhail Nayyar, Gulshan Grover, Mukul Dev, Raghubir Yadav, Brijendra Kala, Sandeep Anand, Supriya Pilgaonkar and Smita Tambe.

In further updates, Of late, it was reported that the movie will not be screened publicly in Nepal, after the country’s Ministry of Communications and Information Technology refused to grant it permission for exhibition. The decision followed a review by Nepal’s Central Movie Censor Board, which found the movie in violation of a provision of the country’s cinema law.

On top of that, A letter was issued by the ministry’s Audio-Visual and Broadcasting Division in which the Central Movie Censor Board examined the movie on Ashwin 19, 2083, as per the Nepali calendar. Following the review, the board concluded that the movie’s production violated Section 8(3) of the National Cinema (Production, Exhibition and Distribution) Act, 2026. Based on the board’s findings, the ministry decided against granting permission for the movie’s public screening in the country.

Udta Teer is produced by Karan Johar, Adar Poonawalla, Apoorva Mehta, Guneet Monga Kapoor and Achin Jain. The project also marks another collaboration between Dharma Productions and Sikhya Entertainment. This marks Ayushmann and Sara's second collaboration after Pati Patni Aur Woh Do. The movie is set to open in cinemas on October 23.

title: Anurag Kashyap, Vasan Bala back Panchayat actors Chandan Roy, Faisal Malik's short film Aakhri Ride, to release on Halloween
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmakers Anurag Kashyap and Vasan Bala have come together to present short movie Aakhri Ride, an atmospheric thriller set to premiere globally on Halloween, October 31. The short movie brings together Panchayat actors Chandan Roy and Faisal Malik, along with Aamir Dalvi, who was part of Kashyap's Kennedy. The movie features the three actors in pivotal roles.

Adding to this, Chandan Roy in a still from Aakhri Ride. About Aakhri Ride Aakhri Ride follows a tense, character-driven narrative centered on a Mumbai ride-share driver pushed to the ultimate edge over the course of one desperate, chilling night.

Meanwhile, The short movie is written and directed by debutants Vijesh Rajan and Yashoda Parthasarthy. It is bankrolled by Ranjan Singh, Vishesh Agrawal, Rajan EPK and Kashyap. The movie will rollout on the YouTube channel Oh Short Flips, which is curated by Kashyap.

Notably, Anurag shared the reason behind backing this movie. He shared, “I have worked with Vijesh and Yashoda from GoW days and always believed they are excellent storytellers with a unique visual language. So when they finally decided to turn writer-directors, it was as an easy decision to back them. And now, I am quite excited to see the audience response to their first movie - Aakhri Ride, when it releases on Halloween Day.”
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Flip Films (@ohflipfilms)

In further updates, Calling the short “quirky and with a beating heart,” Vasan Bala shared, “Vijesh was the Wiz Kid we were introduced to by filmmaker Srinivas. We were always in awe of what he could do with his VFX skills but there there was always a sensitive and fun storyteller in him. When he and Yashoda went to make the movie, we all rooted for them. I was beyond excited to watch their short movie. It’s sharp, fun, quirky and with a beating heart. So coming on board was a nano second decision a no brainer.”

On top of that, Detailing the real-life inspiration behind the movie, writer-directors Vijesh Rajan and Yashoda Parthasarthy added, “Aakhri Ride grew out of our long cab journeys home from meetings across Mumbai. We’d be sitting in the back seat, talking about work or sitting in silence, while the driver was often carrying a completely different world on his phone: family back home, money worries, things we may never fully know. We began to notice an invisible social divide: we were enjoying the comfort of being driven home, while he was trying to make ends meet. We shared a small space, but knew so little about each other’s lives.

“That distance stayed with us, and we wanted to explore it through horror and humour: the idea of a man so consumed by everyday troubles that he doesn’t notice what he’s picked up. We hope viewers laugh, get spooked, and maybe think a little about the person driving them home.”

title: Mika Singh DEFENDS Daler Mehndi amid Uttarakhand event controversy, reveals he had a big operation recently: “Have you ever seen a glass of alcohol in his hand”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

On October 20, Mika shared a video on social media along with a note wishing his followers on Dussehra. He also requested media organisations to check the facts and give artists an opportunity to present their side before reporting allegations.

Adding to this, Mika wrote, “The way Daler Mehndi was treated on stage was disappointing. A respected minister came on stage and made allegations about him drinking alcohol. But before publishing such claims, shouldn’t we verify the facts and give the artist a chance to present his side?” He also questioned whether a similar approach would be taken with an international act, writing, “Would anyone dare to behave like that with an international band like Coldplay?”

Meanwhile, In the video, Mika defended Daler against the allegation that he had been drinking during the performance. He shared, “He has been a superstar for the last 30 years. Have you ever seen a glass of alcohol in his hand in your life?”

Notably, Mika added that Daler has been unwell and is recovering from a recent operation. “If he is not able to stand or he is not able to sing well, he was not feeling well. Because he had a big operation of late,” he shared.

As per the latest buzz, Mika further explained that artists sometimes honour professional commitments despite being unwell. “As much as I get sick, if I come to know that I have a show the day after tomorrow, and I have shared yes, even if the budget was less or more, doesn't matter. I have to be there,” he shared.

In further updates, Daler Mehndi was performing at the annual Siddhpeeth Maa Kunjapuri Tourism and Development Fair in Tehri district on October 18 when Uttarakhand Cabinet Minister and local MLA Subodh Uniyal interrupted the performance.

On top of that, In a video circulating online, Uniyal questioned Mehndi’s ability to sing and alleged that he appeared to be under the influence of alcohol. The minister also questioned the performance in relation to the reported fee.
Mika acknowledged that the minister could question the quality of the performance but objected to the alcohol allegation without proof.

title: Tiger Shroff's team releases first statement after firing attack, warns of legal action over AI-generated videos and fake claims
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

A firing incident involving Tiger Shroff has raised serious concerns in the movie industry and beyond. The incident took place around 7 pm on October 18 in Mumbai , as the Bollywood star was leaving a football club. A video of the shooting showed the attackers opening fire at his car from close range. Tiger escaped without injuries, but his driver and a bystander were as per reports hurt in the incident. The firing has since drawn attention to concerns over the star’s safety, with the incident prompting questions about the circumstances surrounding the attack and the people responsible. Now, the star's team has rolled out first statement.

Adding to this, Team Tiger Shroff issues strong warning against deepfakes and AI-Generated misinformation. (AFP) What the statement says Tiger's team has issued a strong warning against the spread of fake news and AI-generated content falsely linked to the star. In a statement, the team clarified that Tiger has not made any public comments or rolled out videos about a recent incident, and warned that those responsible for spreading misleading content could face legal action.

Meanwhile, The statement comes amid concerns over social media pages and digital platforms using fabricated material to create confusion and spread unverified claims. Team Tiger has urged people to rely on official sources instead of believing or sharing content without checking its authenticity.

Notably, View this post on Instagram The team clarified that the star has not addressed the matter publicly. “We would like to categorically clarify that Tiger Shroff has made no statements, rolled out no videos, and authorised no communication regarding the recent incident or any related developments,” the statement read.

As per the latest buzz, The statement also raised concerns about the misuse of artificial intelligence and the circulation of misleading stories online. According to the team, several platforms have been sharing “fabricated stories, AI-generated videos and scripted narratives, falsely attributed to Tiger.” It described such material as “completely false, unauthorised and intended to mislead the public.”

In further updates, Team Tiger also called on media organisations and digital platforms to exercise caution before publishing or sharing content about the star. The team stressed that it does not support or endorse any of the fabricated material and urged publishers to verify information rather than prioritise clicks or revenue. It asked them to “refrain from creating or amplifying misinformation for engagement or monetary gain.”

On top of that, The statement went on to warn social media users and content creators that sharing such material could have legal consequences. “Any individual or page found creating, promoting or circulating such fabricated content will face appropriate legal action. We are taking cognisance of these instances and reserve the right to pursue all available legal remedies against those responsible,” the notice shared.

The team concluded by asking the public to remain cautious about unverified claims and check information through the star’s official channels. It urged “everyone to rely only on verified communication from Tiger Shroff and his official team.”

title: Prince William calls Karan Johar an ‘icon’, promises to watch Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham after meeting filmmaker in London
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Prince William may soon be catching up on one of Bollywood’s most loved family dramas. The Prince of Wales has called Karan Johar an “icon” and shared he would watch Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham (K3G) after a journalist suggested the movie during a conversation about their recent meeting in London.

Adding to this, Prince William praises Karan Johar’s contribution to Earthshot Prize. The meeting took place during an event linked to the Earthshot Prize , the environmental initiative founded by Prince William and The Royal Foundation. Karan has been helping the project build a stronger presence in India, and the Prince acknowledged his contribution while speaking about their interaction. The conversation took a Bollywood turn when the journalist asked whether William had watched any of the filmmaker’s movies.

Meanwhile, Asked how the meeting went, Prince William had warm words for Johar and his work with the initiative. He told BBC Asian Network, “Really cool. I mean, he's again an icon, and he's been so helpful in kind of being able to help the Earthshot prize land, well in India. We want to make it a truly Indian Earthshot Prize. It's the biggest one we've done.”

Notably, The Prince also referred to Karan as “modest” while discussing his involvement with the project. The journalist then brought up the filmmaker’s movies, pointing out that some of his best-known films have become familiar to audiences well beyond India. William admitted that he had not watched any of his films yet, but seemed open to changing that. He replied, “No, he's being very modest. But I'm sure as time goes on, he'll introduce some more films to me.”

As per the latest buzz, The journalist had a specific recommendation in mind: Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham, the 2001 family drama starring Amitabh Bachchan, Jaya Bachchan, Shah Rukh Khan, Kajol, Hrithik Roshan and Kareena Kapoor Khan. Encouraging William to give it a watch, the journalist shared: “Yeah, we all say K3G anyway. If you meet Karan again, 'Tell him, I'm going to watch your movie K3G, he'll love you.'” William agreed, saying: “Okay got it, I'll mention that too when I see him.”

In further updates, View this post on Instagram What is happening at the Earthshot Prize in India? The Earthshot Prize Summit will bring together people from across business, environmental innovation, funding and community organisations for two days of discussions and collaboration. The aim is to connect promising environmental projects with the resources and partnerships they need to grow.

On top of that, The summit will lead up to the sixth Earthshot Prize Awards Night on November 17, 2026. Fifteen finalists will be recognised, with five winners set to receive £1 million each to help develop and expand their solutions. The initiative focuses on supporting ideas that can make a meaningful difference to the planet.

Away from his Earthshot Prize work, Johar has several projects keeping him busy. His star chat show Koffee with Karan is nearing the end of its run. Following the premiere of season 9 with Salman Khan, Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna are also set to appear on the show while promoting their movie Ranabaali.

title: Nick Jonas gets candid about Jonas Brothers’ split with mother-in-law Madhu Chopra, recalls being in a ‘pressure cooker’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Nick Jonas of late sat down with his mother-in-law, Madhu Chopra , mother of Priyanka Chopra, for a conversation in which he opened up about the reasons behind the Jonas Brothers ' split in 2013 and their eventual reunion in 2019. The singer also reflected on a personal flaw he has recognised in himself.

Adding to this, Nick Jonas spoke about his one flaw to Madhu Chopra, (Instagram) Nick Jonas opens up about being in a 'pressure cooker' during early years of success Although Nick's podcast conversation with Madhu Chopra is yet to be rolled out, she shared a few clips from the interview on social media. In one of the clips, Nick discussed the factors that led to the Jonas Brothers' breakup.

Meanwhile, “There was a fraying that was happening. From our last album till the time we broke up, it was a combination of growing up, being in a pressure cooker of having reached this level of success and having not quite reached that success for a number of years, finding that we weren't extending our collaborators because we were afraid that maybe if we reached out, people wouldn't want to work with us,” he shared.

Notably, View this post on Instagram Nick Jonas reveals the one flaw he sees in himself During the conversation, Madhu lauded Nick for balancing his responsibilities as a father, husband and rockstar. She then asked him to identify the one flaw he sees in himself. Responding to her question, Nick shared, “You should probably ask that to your daughter.”

As per the latest buzz, He went on to explain that his biggest flaw is his tendency to overthink certain aspects of the creative process. “My major flaw is my tendency to overthink certain things in the creative process and I always describe it as I am tightening the screw until eventually the wood breaks and you reach a sweet spot where you are giving as much effort as you can but you can also overcook it. So, just find that perfect balance where you have done your best that you feel you can do and leave it in the hands of others,” he shared.

In further updates, View this post on Instagram 4:59 embed 2 View this post on Instagram About the Jonas Brothers The Jonas Brothers, comprising brothers Nick Jonas, Joe Jonas and Kevin Jonas, rose to fame with their music in the 2000s. The band revealed its split in 2013 amid creative differences and tensions among the brothers.

On top of that, After pursuing individual projects, the trio reunited in 2019, marking their comeback with the single Sucker. The song became a major hit and signalled a new chapter for the band as the brothers returned to making music together.

title: ‘Tired of spreading lies’: BJP takes dig at Rahul Gandhi over foreign trip amid protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Tuesday took a dig at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his foreign trips, alleging that he had left for another overseas visit amid the Opposition’s ongoing protests.

Adding to this, Taking a dig at the Congress leader, the ruling party suggested that he was tired of the protests and had taken a break. (X/@BJP4India) The ruling party shared a video on X, as per reports filmed by a fellow passenger, which purportedly showed Gandhi aboard a flight to Vietnam. Taking a swipe at the Congress leader, the BJP suggested that he was taking a break from the protests.
Meanwhile, "I'm tired of spreading lies... Let me go roam around Vietnam for a few days... Who the hell would even find out!” BJP shared on X.

Notably, The official handle of BJP Goa also took a dig at Gandhi. Tagging INC handle on X, it shared, “To ‘RECOVER’ from yesterday's FLOP yatra and that 10-minute walk in Goa organised by your 'Non-Dimaagi Naxals' Goa Congress, the clown is already tired and escaping to Vietnam.”
As per the latest buzz, BJP accused the Congress leader of creating chaos, fueling anarchy and running away for vacation and hoped for him to have a “colourful” time.

In further updates, “His business model is clear: Create chaos in India, fuel anarchy, and run away for vacation. Part-time anarchy, full-time vacation - that's his job profile. Anyway, hope he enjoys his colourful time there,” it added on X.

On top of that, BJP MP Praveen Khandelwal claimed that this was not the first time Gandhi had travelled abroad. He accused the Congress leader of “creating a row” in India before leaving on foreign trips.

"Rahul Gandhi is not doing this for the first time. He often spends more time travelling abroad. His only job is to come to India, create a row over an issue and then leave on foreign trips. Where does he go abroad and whom does he meet? Nobody understands this, and nobody knows,” he told news agency PTI .

title: Protests barred at 3 Bhopal sites for 2 months, no alternative site designated
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Police have prohibited sit-ins, demonstrations, agitations, strikes, and burning of effigies at three popular protest spots in Bhopal for the next two months without designating any alternative place.

Adding to this, Bhopal police commissioner Sanjay Kumar declared the three sites and the stretches between them as restricted zones. Bhopal police commissioner Sanjay Kumar declared Polytechnic Square, Akashvani Square, Kilol Park Square, and the stretches between them as restricted zones for protests under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) Section 163.

Meanwhile, In the order issued on Monday, Kumar shared these intersections lie on the main road leading to important places like the airport, Hamidia Hospital and Gandhi Medical College. It added that it is the only convenient route and there is no alternative. “Frequent applications are received from communities, organisations, political parties, committees and delegations to hold dharna, protest, demonstrations, agitations and effigy burning at Polytechnic Square, which disrupts traffic and causes severe inconvenience to the public.”

Notably, The order cited the movement of emergency services like ambulances and fire brigades and VIPs and VVIPs and shared the agitations, protests and demonstrations could endanger the lives of patients due to delays. It added that, therefore, it appears necessary to declare the area as a restricted zone.

As per the latest buzz, Kumar exercised powers under Section 163 (1) of BNSS and prohibited all such programmes in the area. His order under Section 163 (2) of BNSS will remain in force for two months from the date of implementation. It shared any violation will attract action.

In further updates, Opposition Congress leader Anand Jat accused the Bharatiya Janata Party government of suppressing people’s voices by issuing such an order. “They are now afraid of people’s voice, but these restrictions will not stop people from raising their voice,” shared Jat.

On top of that, Tens of thousands of people this month took to the streets in Delhi seeking chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll and demanded the scrapping of the exercise.

Authorities ordered Metro closures, Internet shutdowns, imposed prohibitory orders and deployed 40,000 security personnel to turn Delhi into a virtual fortress. Many protesters were dragged, manhandled, and detained.

title: Ranbir Kapoor surprises Hyderabad fans with Telugu speech at pre-release Ramayana event: ‘I hope I have not said anything wrong’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ranbir Kapoor made a special effort to connect with his Telugu-speaking followers at the Hyderabad event for Ramayana : Rise of a Legend on Monday. The star, who will be seen as Lord Rama in Nitesh Tiwari’s soon-to-release movie, surprised the audience by addressing them in Telugu. His attempt was met with loud cheers, while co-star Sai Pallavi, who plays Sita, watched with a smile.

Adding to this, 11. Ranbir Kapoor promises a grand cinematic experience at Ramayana event, thanks Telugu followers in their language. The event was organised ahead of the movie's theatrical rollout in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, where it will be distributed by Dil Raju's Sri Venkateswara Creations (SVC). With its ambitious scale and a star cast led by Ranbir, Sai Pallavi and Yash, the movie has been building anticipation among audiences.

Meanwhile, At the event, Ranbir first spoke in English, thanking followers for accepting him and his work. He assured them that he would give his best to make the movie a memorable experience in theatres. He shared, “To all my Telugu-speaking friends, all my brothers and sisters from all over the world. I want to thank you for accepting me and my work. I will promise that I will always work hard so that I can give you all some cinematic experience on the big screen.”

Notably, He then continued in Telugu, earning an enthusiastic response from the audience. "Hyderabad ku raavadam naaku epudu pratyekame. Mee prema, abhimaanam naaku chala villuvenavi (Coming to Hyderabad is always special for me. Your love and affection are very valuable to me)," he continued.

As per the latest buzz, Keeping the moment light-hearted, Ranbir added, "I hope I have not shared anything wrong." Sai Pallavi appeared delighted by his effort to speak to the crowd in their language.

In further updates, During his address, Ranbir spoke about the values at the heart of the epic and what audiences could expect from the movie. He described Ramayana as a story that continues to resonate across generations, going beyond its place in mythology.

On top of that, “Jai Shri Ram! Greetings to everyone. Some stories do not need to be told because they live on with us. Ramayana is one such story. Ramayana is a wonderful journey that teaches us how to be a great father, a good son, a loving husband and a true friend. When you watch this movie, it will not feel like you are simply watching a movie. You will undoubtedly experience something extraordinary. This is a movie that inspires goodness in all of us."

He added, “Namit Malhotra has brought this movie to life with an extraordinary vision. Director Nitesh Tiwari has crafted it beautifully, and I thank him for making me a part of this movie. Rakul’s performance in this movie is very different and will surprise all of you. My journey with Sai Pallavi on this movie has been a memorable experience. Whenever I saw her on the sets, I genuinely felt as though I was looking at Goddess Sita herself. I cannot imagine anyone other than her playing this character. If I had a brother, he would be like Ravi. Rocking Star Yash is a wonderful family man. He left his family, his city and everything behind to be a part of Ramayana. I have never seen anyone work as hard as he does.”

title: Screenwriter Apurva Asrani says he won’t be surprised if people are thrown into Tihar jail for disliking Ramayana
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Yash of late urged audiences not to nitpick the VFX in Ramayana and extend their full support to the much-awaited movie, which stars him as Ravana and Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama. Now, screenwriter Apurva Asrani, known for critically acclaimed films such as Shahid and Aligarh, seemingly criticised Yash's comments, comparing them to a sign of dictatorship.

Adding to this, Ramayana will rollout worldwide on November 5. ‘Won’t be surprised if they throw us in Tihar Jail for disliking the movie’ Apurva took to X (formerly Twitter) and wrote, “I won’t be surprised if they throw us in friggin’ Tihar Jail for disliking the new Ramayana, refusing to bang a thali to solve the oil crisis, or daring to eat a chicken burger on a Tuesday. Maybe even for switching off the TV during the supreme leader’s speech.”

Meanwhile, Apurva went on to link Yash's comments to the India's current political climate. He also referred to the arrest of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who have been held in Delhi's Tihar Jail for allegedly trespassing and entering the Jantar Mantar protest site after it was removed from the list of authorised demonstration venues.

Notably, Apurva wrote, “That’s how far down the road to dictatorship India is sliding. Watching how Saurav & Ashutosh are being treated, it is sad to see how the Constitution of India has been reduced to a mockery. Raise your voice now, before even a joke, a question or the slightest disagreement becomes grounds for state retaliation.”

As per the latest buzz, At a recent Ramayana pre-rollout event in Hyderabad, Yash urged audiences to support the movie and refrain from nitpicking over its visual effects. He also shared India needed to protect filmmakers such as producer Namit Malhotra, who are striving to take Indian cinema to a global platform.

In further updates, Yash shared, “Anybody can dream of making a movie, but only a few people will have that kind of passion, dedication, determination and madness. As an Indian, I am telling you, we need to protect this guy. It's our responsibility because this man was comfortably doing business in LA. Every time I met him, he always spoke about one thing, ‘We all are doing so much and Indians have done so much, but we should do something for our Indian movie industry and I want to do it. I am getting Oscars, but I am not happy. I want our country to be placed at that level and that's the day I am going to be happy.’ This is what he told me.”
On top of that, Earlier, at Ramayana's trailer launch event in Bengaluru, Yash verified that the two-part epic has a combined budget of ₹ 4,000 crore rupees.

title: 30-foot cockroach effigy in Delhi to be burnt alongside Ravana on Dussehra amid CJP protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

A 30-foot-tall cockroach effigy has been put up in Delhi's Pitampura to be burnt alongside the traditional effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnad on Dussehra. The move is seen as a jibe at the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), which has been protesting over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Adding to this, The installation comes amid protests by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) in the national capital although the committe has denied any political motivation. (ANI Screengrab) CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke reacted to a video of the effigy shared by news agency ANI, writing, “Thank you for the free publicity.” The video showed the cockroach figure standing alongside the traditional effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnad, which are burnt during the festival.

Meanwhile, CJP legal head Ratna Singh also commented on the installation, writing, “Tamasha Kara lo bas is desh mein” (Just keep putting on a spectacle in this country). Both leaders' remarks drew reactions on social media, with several users linking the proposed burning of the cockroach effigy to the triumph of good over evil.

Notably, The Shree Keshav Ramlila Committee, which erected the effigy, has shared the move is not politically motivated. Committee president and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA Ashok Goel told news agency PTI that the cockroach represents filth and dirt, and that burning it is intended to promote cleanliness under the Swachh Bharat and Swachh Delhi campaigns.
As per the latest buzz, “Our goal is to eliminate filth from three areas: our homes, our immediate surroundings and society at large,” Goel shared.
In further updates, He added that the committee has introduced additional effigies to highlight social issues in previous years, including figures representing Naxalism and terrorism.

On top of that, The CJP has been staging protests in the national capital over various issues. The group initially demonstrated against former education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and later joined protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

In June and July, CJP members staged a protest at Jantar Mantar for more than a month before marching towards Parliament on July 20. The group has since joined opposition parties and student organisations in demonstrations over alleged irregularities in the SIR of electoral rolls.

title: Protesters must focus on solutions, not divisions: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat on Tuesday shared that protesters must focus on finding constructive solutions rather than creating divisions in society as he addressed a range of social concerns and global challenges at the annual Vijayadashami event

Adding to this, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat in Nagpur on Tuesday. (ANI) His reference to the protests came against the backdrop of the Cockroach Janta Party and the Congress’s agitations demanding the chief election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s removal. Tens of thousands of people have taken to the streets seeking Kumar’s removal and the scrapping of the electoral roll Special Intensive Revision (SIR) over alleged irregularities.

Meanwhile, Speaking at the RSS headquarters in Nagpur on the occasion of the organisation’s 101st anniversary, he cited protests in India and Western countries, describing them as part of a disruptive cultural storm coming from the West that opposes systemic conduct and institutional security. “We are hearing such news from France. We know what happened in Nepal, Bangladesh too,” he shared. “Such things are happening in India too, but a problem is rarely solved with agitation.”

Notably, Bhagwat accused certain global powers and domestic forces of actively trying to weaken India and exploit social differences. He urged people not to let cheap publicity overcome their wisdom, emphasising that national unity and society’s rise as a whole provide the best solutions.

As per the latest buzz, Bhagwat shared that changing governments or regimes has historically never resolved a country’s deep-seated problems, citing past and present political upheavals in nations to illustrate his point. He noted similar agitational politics is happening in India.

In further updates, Bhagwat cautioned that it is extremely rare for complex societal problems to be solved purely through street agitations. He alleged that certain narrow-minded global powers and domestic political opponents are actively trying to weaken India. Bhagwat shared that these external and internal forces exploit existing social differences, amplify feelings of victimhood and public dissatisfaction, and attempt to distance citizens from the collective social order.

On top of that, He shared such efforts are designed to foster hatred toward governance systems and create widespread disorder. Bhagwat observed with satisfaction that the younger generation is displaying a growing sense of national pride, which he shared has become a matter of concern for forces seeking to dismantle India’s stability.

Bhagwat called for an immediate and strict ban on drugs and narcotics, announcing that the RSS will actively work on combating this menace. He advocated for the proper regulation of OTT content to safeguard cultural values and protect younger audiences.

title: SCOOP: Ramayana advance booking may get DELAYED due to revenue-sharing tussle; distributors demand 60% share in Week 1
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

A trade source told Bollywood Hungama, “Usually, for big films, the distributor's share is 52.5% in Week 1, 45% in Week 2 and 37.5% in Week 3. But the distributors of Ramayana are as per reports demanding a 60% revenue share in the first week, 50% in the second week and 40% in the third week. This is significantly higher than the usual sharing terms followed for big-budget films. As a result, exhibitors, who are understandably concerned, are reluctant to agree to these terms and negotiations are currently underway.”

Adding to this, The source continued, “Unless both parties arrive at a mutually acceptable agreement, the advance booking could get delayed. Everyone is keen to rollout Ramayana on a grand scale, but there has to be mutual consensus when it comes to commercial terms.”

Meanwhile, It remains to be seen whether the two sides can resolve their differences soon and ensure that advance bookings begin across the country. As of 9:30 am, INOX Korum Mall in Thane is the only cinema in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region to have opened bookings for Ramayana. Another prominent multiplex where advance bookings have commenced is AMB Cinemas Kapali in Bengaluru.

title: HT Exclusive | Anurag Kashyap says only devotional or patriotic films are being greenlit in Bollywood, making films is difficult today
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Many are calling 2026 the year of patriotic and devotional films in Hindi cinema. With the success of movies like Dhurandhar and Hanuman Ansh, there is a wave of patriotic and devotional titles being revealed. Filmmaker Anurag Kashyap believes that the two genres now have hegemony in Bollywood, with other diverse genres struggling to even surface. In a chat with Hindustan Times, the filmmaker opens up on why making diverse films is challenging these days.

Adding to this, Anurag Kashyap opens up on the state of Indian cinema. Anurag Kashyap on devotional and patriotic films Anurag is backing the independently made children’s movie Little Thomas , starring Gulshan Devaiah and Rasika Dugal, and directed by Kaushal Oza. Talking about his role as an executive producer, Anurag says, “I see myself more as an enabler.”

Meanwhile, The filmmaker elaborates, “It is just about faith and upping somebody’s morale. I see myself as someone who keeps morale high and helps them complete and rollout a movie. I don’t think anybody knows what to make today. Movie banana hi difficult hai (It is difficult to make films). Whether it’s a children’s movie or an adult movie, making your own movie is difficult today.”

Notably, Anurag says the wave of patriotic and devotional films being revealed shows that Hindi cinema is now following that trend. He explains, “I was talking to a producer the other day, and they shared, ‘We don’t know what to do’. You can make either a patriotic or a devotional movie. Otherwise, nothing else is getting greenlit. That is a fact and a tragedy.”

As per the latest buzz, Three of the four biggest hits from Bollywood this year fit in this bracket - Dhurandhar 2, Hanuman Ansh, and Border 2. Several more have since been revealed. But Anurag feels that this also creates an environment ripe for slice-of-life films like Little Thomas. “Hopefully, this movie will sneak in, because this is not like any other movie out there,” he says.

In further updates, The filmmaker also feels that merely because some films have children as protagonists does not make them kids’ films. “For instance, what will you call this recent Telugu movie called Don’t Trouble The Trouble, which stars Fahadh Faasil and is backed by SS Rajamouli. It has Fahadh, so would you call it a children’s movie?” he argues. Conversely, he shares an argument from the other end of the spectrum. “When we go to festivals, we see so many coming-of-age films. The biggest, most talked-about series in the last two years was Adolescence. But they are for adults,” says Anurag.

On top of that, Written and directed by Kaushal Oza, Little Thomas features an ensemble cast led by Gulshan Devaiah and Rasika Dugal and also features child artiste Hridansh Parekh in the titular role. The movie is produced by Anurag Kashyap, alongside Anushka Shah, Charu Oza, Rajnikant Oza, Akshay Thakker, Kabir Ahuja, and Ranjan Singh. It is slated for a theatrical rollout on October 23.

A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. title: Sharad Kelkar says he spoke to Tiger Shroff after firing incident, trusts Mumbai Police to get to the bottom of the case
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The Hindi movie industry was shaken after a firing incident involving Tiger Shroff on Sunday. Shots were fired at the star as he left a football club in Mumbai. While the star escaped unhurt, he did suffer gunpowder burns on his right hand. Of late, star Sharad Kelkar reacted to the incident and called out the 'anarchy in the country'.He also expressed faith in Mumbai Police to get to the bottom of the incident.

Adding to this, Sharad Kelkar spoke about Tiger Shroff firing incident. 'Should never be this kind of anarchy in the country' In conversation with ANI, Sharad Kelkar shared, "It's not just about Bollywood or any famous person. There should never be this kind of anarchy in the country. The Mumbai Police is very on top of things, and everyone has been caught."

Meanwhile, The Tanhaji star also shared that he spoke to Tiger after the incident and assured his followers that he is doing fine. He shared, "And yesterday I even spoke to Jackie Shroff, sent him a message. So everything is alright, it's safe. But yes, what happened was wrong, but I have full faith in the Mumbai Police—they have already caught the culprits, and they will get to the bottom of this."

Notably, Along with Sharad, celebrities like Vidyut Jammwal, Ram Gopal Varma, filmmaker Rahul Dholakia and others also reacted to the incident. Vidyut posted on Instagram on Monday and expressed his concern over the firing incident. He called Tiger "the most fearless person". He also questioned Mumbai Police about the lapse in Tiger's security. He shared, “I would like to tell the Mumbai Police: you have provided him with security, but this must never happen again. If a lapse like this occurs, then you are the ones at fault."

As per the latest buzz, After the firing incident, Mumbai Police arrested three men accused of targeting Tiger Shroff’s car in Mumbai. They were arrested in Rajasthan's Kota on Monday. As per reports, the arrests came after an overnight search involving multiple police teams across states.

In further updates, The accused have been identified as Hritik alias Roshan, from Begusarai in Bihar, Rehan from Sonipat in Haryana, and a third associate. They were arrested from the general coach of the Pune-Jaipur Superfast Express when the train reached Kota railway station at 10:17 am, Kota Superintendent of Police Tejaswani Gautam shared. The police are also probing the alleged Lawrence Bishnoi gang link in the firing incident.

title: Ramayana's Kumbhakarna used Mark Ruffalo's Hulk as reference, reveals Faisal Malik: 'He's massive'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

We have seen giants on screen in The Lord of the Rings and other fantasy franchises. Over the last two decades, Hulk has come to define brute strength on the big screen, with Mark Ruffalo ’s portrayal of the character in the Marvel Cinematic Universe becoming widely lauded. In fact, such is the reverence for the character that star Faisal Malik based his portrayal of the asura Kumbhakarna in Ramayana on him.

Adding to this, Faisal Malik (right) says his Kumbhakarna uses Mark Ruffalo's Hulk as a reference. Faisal Malik on Kumbhakaran In a recent interview with Variety India, Faisal Malik opened up on playing Kumbhakarna in Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana. The trailers of the movie have given a good glimpse at the gigantic size of the asura and Ravana’s brother. In the epic, Kumbhakarna is described as 600 bows in height, which could imply a height of 1800-2400 feet. Talking about transforming into the behemoth, Faisal shared, “We have all seen the Hulk and how Mark Ruffalo becomes the big green guy. That is a reference for me when I started imagining how I would look.”

Meanwhile, Best known for playing Prahlad Cha in Panchayat, Faisal has also appeared in small parts in films such as Gangs of Wasseypur. Ramayana’s Kumbhakarna is his highest-profile role yet. Talking about the experience, he added, “My experience of playing Kumbhakarna in Ramayana is a dream come true. We grew up watching Ramayana, so playing a character from it feels like sheer luck. The challenge here is that this world is completely different for me. He isn't a normal human; he's massive, and he was in a deep sleep for six months. To keep all of that in mind and derive a final output is a tricky part.”
Notably, Nalin Dave played Kumbhakarna in Ramanand Sagar’s 1987 TV series, Ramayan. It is considered one of the most defining portrayals of the character.

As per the latest buzz, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The first part is scheduled for worldwide rollout on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2027. The films will rollout in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam across India.

In further updates, Sony Pictures will handle global distribution, excluding India, while Dharma Productions will distribute the movie in the Hindi-speaking market. The movie is also planned for a worldwide IMAX rollout.

title: Tanishaa Mukerji calls Bigg Boss a game of manipulation, says she was brainwashed into relationship with Armaan Kohli
body: Here's the latest relationship update doing the rounds:

Bigg Boss has often been a breeding ground for drama, unexpected romances and relationships that keep viewers hooked. During the seventh season of the reality show, star Tanishaa Mukerji , sister of Kajol , grew close to fellow contestant Armaan Kohli . Years later, Tanishaa has opened up about the relationship in a recent podcast, describing Bigg Boss as a game of manipulation and claiming she was ‘brainwashed’ into getting involved with Armaan.

Adding to this, Tanishaa Mukerji and Armaan Kohli participated in Bigg Boss 7. Tanishaa Mukerji on relationship with Armaan Kohli In a chat with YouTube channel Unfolding Humans, Tanishaa shared she had entered Bigg Boss without fully understanding what she was getting into. She admitted that she had been naive and unprepared for the experience, adding that people should approach the reality show with a better understanding of the show. She also shared that relationships and friendships in life stem from karmic connections and advised people to be cautious while participating in Bigg Boss.

Meanwhile, She explained that the Bigg Boss team puts people in certain situations to make two people feel like a team and loyal to each other. Tanishaa added, "They manipulate you into these things. They put you together in dump situations, in jail together, so again you are sympathising with each other over your misery. All these experiences build fake emotions in you which are not really yours. The emotions that have been built up are because of the experiences you have had together, which, again, you didn’t choose to have. These are the situations determined by the people controlling the game show. These are the things I realised later."

Notably, She claimed that the makers subsequently placed her and Armaan in the same team, creating more opportunities for them to interact. Tanishaa shared she felt an immediate sense of familiarity with Armaan Kohli because he, too, came from a movie industry family. She added that she found it easy to be around him because he had a movie industry vibe that nobody else in the house shared.

As per the latest buzz, She added, "And then the situations put us into those moments where there was a lot of trauma bonding. After I came out, I had to go to a psychiatrist. It took me six months to break out of Bigg Boss brainwashing. You have to be very careful when you go into these reality shows, and today kids are a lot more sorted. I think it is because of the background I come from, as I was living in a bubble. I was in a very live-and-let-live, easy space. I didn’t experience manipulation until I entered the Bigg Boss house."

In further updates, Armaan and Tanishaa's relationship began during their stint on Bigg Boss 7 in 2013. Their closeness on the reality show, including their romantic moments frequently made headlines. After the show ended, the couple continued to be linked romantically, with Armaan describing Tanishaa as an important part of his life. However, their relationship ended in 2014, after dating for about a year. Tanishaa later shared that they were very different people with different ideologies.
